name: F-1-D Workation (digital nomad) visa

requirement_groups.name: Remote worker for a foreign employer

requirements.blocker_text: Requires ongoing employment with, or self-employment through, a company based outside Korea; the visa does not authorise work for a Korean employer or client.
requirements.fix_path: Confirm the employing or contracting entity is genuinely foreign-based and the work is performed remotely for that entity.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires annual income of at least twice Korea's per-capita Gross National Income (GNI), a materially higher bar than comparable digital-nomad visas in Southeast Asia -- KRW 104,832,000/year based on the Bank of Korea's 10 March 2026 announcement of 2025 per-capita GNI (KRW 52,416,000).
requirements.fix_path: Document income at or above the current 2x-GNI threshold from the foreign employer or client base.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires private health insurance covering the full intended stay in Korea (Korea's national health insurance is not available to F-1-D holders).
requirements.fix_path: Purchase qualifying private health insurance for the intended stay duration.

evidence_required.document: Employment or client contracts with foreign-based entities showing the qualifying income
Private health insurance certificate covering the stay

sources.title: HiKorea -- Korea Immigration Service's official portal for visa categories, ARC, and stay procedures
Bank of Korea (bok.or.kr) -- official press release archive; 10 March 2026 release confirming 2025 per-capita GNI of KRW 52,416,000
LegalClarity -- How to Immigrate to South Korea: Visas, Residency & Citizenship, corroborating the 2x-GNI income threshold and January 2024 launch date

notes: Launched January 2024, F-1-D is a genuinely narrow product by design: work_rights is 'restricted' rather than 'full' because the entire premise of the visa is that all income-generating activity must flow to a foreign entity -- any Korean-sourced income or Korean-client work falls outside its scope entirely, a sharper boundary than most other countries' digital-nomad products in this dataset. The 2x-GNI income bar is explicitly and repeatedly described across sources as significantly higher than comparable Southeast Asian digital-nomad visas, positioning F-1-D as a high-income-only product rather than a broadly accessible remote-work route. switchable_to is empty because F-1-D does not lead anywhere in the route graph -- it is a standalone, capped-duration status structurally similar to Poland's Schengen visitor route or the UAE's Green Visa in shape, not a stepping stone toward settlement. formula_ref uses the 'gni_x2' key defined in national-variables/KR.json, this build's first Korea national-variables file -- created specifically because this route and kr_f5_permanent_residence both peg income thresholds to the same underlying GNI figure, the same formula_ref pattern used for Poland's GUS-linked thresholds elsewhere in this dataset. A genuine within-year figure revision is worth flagging: BOK's 10 March 2026 preliminary announcement gave KRW 52,416,000 for 2025 per-capita GNI; a later 9 June 2026 release restated it as KRW 52,570,000. This route uses the March figure as the operative value -- see national-variables/KR.json for the full reasoning.
